BR-01.text: Every reported case figure (closed, resolved, cost, handling time) shall declare which definition of the state it uses, and figures built on

BR-02.text: The organisation shall record who decides the definition of closed/resolved and the closure-time expectation. The engagement shall not choos

BR-03.text: Time-to-close shall be measurable under each candidate definition (elapsed from receipt to ops-closed, and to evidence-complete) without pre

BR-04.text: Externally received case information shall be matched to exactly one core case, or flagged unmatched, before it reaches a reviewer's queue.

BR-05.text: A re-delivered or replayed item shall not increase the exception queue or alter totals.

BR-06.text: Delayed, missing or revised items shall be detectable and attributable to a source and time without manual spreadsheet reconciliation.

BR-07.text: Each case decision shall carry the evidence relied on and its source, retrievable on request.

BR-08.text: Batch disposition and any other decision requiring an authorised person shall remain a human decision; no process shall make, pre-fill as fi

BR-09.text: No case shall be closed without verifiable evidence unless an owner has explicitly authorised an exception rule.

BR-10.text: Case cost and avoidable rework shall be attributable per case and per period using one agreed cut-off and denominator.

BR-11.text: Existing legitimate workflows (including the parallel path for older customers) shall not be disrupted without an identified owner's agreeme

BR-12.text: Backlog ageing and unresolved exception rate shall be visible per site and comparable across sites.

BR-13.text: Change to the handling process shall be releasable without causing a rollback of the kind documented in 2025.

RC-1.text: The step that records a case decision, closure or batch disposition (with actor and basis) has no representation in the system. The only wri

RC-2.text: Case state is a mutable snapshot: `cases.version` = 1 for 125/125 with no code that increments it; creation event stores the *current* statu

RC-3.text: No owned definition of "closed / resolved / approved", and no decider for the speed-vs-evidence trade-off (DR-20, DR-21, DR-23 are GAPs; `op

RC-4.text: The approval/priority logic exists as three unsynchronised implementations: `app/legacy_logic.py` (>50,000), `legacy_js/legacy_policy.js` (r

RC-5.text: Execution is manual-start, capacity-capped and unrecorded: no scheduler anywhere; `reconcile(limit=1000)` vs 8,567 backlog rows (9 runs); re

RC-6.text: Intake is destructive and content-blind: reconcile overwrites `processing_status` in place; every REPLAY becomes DUPLICATE without content c

RC-7.text: No shared identity or referential model: `cases` has no batch/deviation/CAPA/feed key; `partner_feeds.ref_id` has no FK; five status vocabul

RC-8.text: Month-end figures are computed independently without a shared definition: SQL `LEFT JOIN events` inflates `SUM(amount)` by 19.3% on the ship

SUC-04.text: Time to close under D-OPS and under D-EVID, reported separately

SUC-09.text: Backlog ageing and unresolved exception rate
